intro: YouTubers I applaud for proving that value beats production. Simple setups, little visual polish, and huge audiences, because what they say is worth the time.

creators.name: Sabine Hossenfelder
creators.who: A theoretical physicist who covers science and technology news.
style: Mostly her, talking to camera, with few visuals
Skeptical and direct: says when the hype is wrong
creators.lesson: Expertise plus honesty is the product. 'The data says otherwise' is exactly your Pillar 2 voice, and it doesn't need a studio.

creators.name: Dr. Todd Grande
creators.who: A licensed counselor (PhD) who explains psychology and mental-health topics.
style: A plain setup: one camera, one desk
Very consistent, one topic per video
creators.lesson: Consistency and clarity beat polish. One clear topic per video, explained well, over and over.

you.label: 🧑‍✈️ Aim here
you.note: High value, low-to-medium production: your knowledge and energy carry the video. Spend the saved time on the next video.

whyItMatters.title: Ship more, polish less
whyItMatters.detail: Quick Start 9 and Follow Thru 2: heavy editing is where your videos stall. A simple setup means more videos actually get published.

whyItMatters.title: Your own data agrees
whyItMatters.detail: Your best recent uploads, the cheap-model Kilo Shorts (185–195 views), won on a useful, copyable idea, not on production budget.

whyItMatters.title: Value is the hook
whyItMatters.detail: Titles and the first 30 seconds promise a payoff, and the content delivers it. That matters more than B-roll or motion graphics.

whyItMatters.title: Credibility over cinematics
whyItMatters.detail: They're trusted for what they know (a physicist, a counsellor). For you it's 40+ delivered contracts, 612 repos and real delivery work.

rules: 🎥 The default setup: one camera or screen recording, good audio, and a clear title
⏱️ Cap editing time per video. If it's taking longer, publish and improve the next one
🎯 One topic per video, with the payoff in the first 30 seconds
🔊 Spend on audio first. Viewers forgive simple visuals, but not bad sound
